concepts.name: Virtual File System (VFS) & Inode Mechanics
concepts.description: The VFS layer abstracts underlying physical file systems. Inodes store file metadata (permissions, ownership, size, data block pointers) independently of filenames.
concepts.production_usage: Essential when diagnosing 'No space left on device' errors where disk space is reported available but 100% of inodes are exhausted due to millions of small session/cache files.

concepts.name: Process Lifecycle, States (R, S, D, Z) & Signal Handling
concepts.description: Processes transition between Running (R), Interruptible Sleep (S), Uninterruptible Sleep (D - usually disk/NFS wait), and Zombie (Z). Controlled via signals like SIGTERM (15) and SIGKILL (9).
concepts.production_usage: Used in graceful blue-green deployment terminations where orchestrators wait for in-flight requests to complete before force-killing stuck processes.

concepts.name: Virtual Memory, Page Cache & OOM Killer
concepts.description: Linux utilizes available RAM for page caching. When memory pressure exceeds physical RAM and swap, the OOM Killer invokes oom_badness() to terminate the highest-consuming process.
concepts.production_usage: SREs tune /proc/sys/vm/swappiness and set oom_score_adj on production databases to guarantee protection against unexpected OS terminations.

concepts.name: Systemd Architecture & cgroup Integration
concepts.description: PID 1 init system providing parallel service activation, dependency tracking, socket activation, and strict cgroup resource constraints.
concepts.production_usage: Standardizing enterprise daemon deployment with automated restart policies, CPU quotas, and strict memory limits.

concepts.name: TCP 3-Way Handshake & Socket Lifecycle
concepts.description: Connection establishment via SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK. Teardown via FIN/ACK sequences. States include ESTABLISHED, TIME_WAIT (waiting for delayed packets), and CLOSE_WAIT (remote closed, local app has not closed socket).
concepts.production_usage: CLOSE_WAIT accumulation indicates application resource leaks (open HTTP/database clients not calling close()), while excessive TIME_WAIT exhausts ephemeral ports under high connection churn.

concepts.name: DNS Resolution Hierarchy & Query Mechanics
concepts.description: Step-by-step resolution from client stub resolver (/etc/resolv.conf) to local caching resolver, root DNS servers, TLD name servers, and authoritative name servers.
concepts.production_usage: In Kubernetes, ndots:5 configuration issues cause high CoreDNS latency by appending search domains up to 5 times for external FQDNs unless trailing dots are used.

concepts.name: Connection Tracking (conntrack) & NAT
concepts.description: Linux netfilter subsystem tracking state for every bidirectional network stream. Required for stateful firewalling and Kubernetes kube-proxy iptables service routing.
concepts.production_usage: When conntrack table fills up (nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet), nodes drop all new TCP connections. Requires tuning nf_conntrack_max and hash size.

concepts.name: TLS/SSL Cryptographic Handshake & PKI
concepts.description: Asymmetric key exchange (ECDHE) and certificate validation against trusted Certificate Authorities (CAs), followed by symmetric session encryption (AES-GCM/ChaCha20).
concepts.production_usage: Automating cert-manager rotation in production to avoid catastrophic outages caused by expired wildcard SSL/TLS certificates.

troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Update security group inbound rules, verify host firewall (ufw status), and check route table default gateways.

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: High DNS Latency in Kubernetes Microservices

troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Inspect `/etc/resolv.conf` in pod, query with `dig +trace`, and monitor CoreDNS request duration metrics.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Append a trailing dot to external URLs (e.g. `api.stripe.com.`) or adjust pod dnsConfig ndots:2.

concepts.name: Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) & Object Model
concepts.description: Git stores data as content-addressable objects in `.git/objects` identified by SHA-1/SHA-256 hashes: Blobs (file contents), Trees (directory structures), Commits (pointers to trees and parent commits), and Annotated Tags.
concepts.production_usage: Understanding the DAG prevents fear of rebasing or resetting; as long as an object was committed, it exists in the object store and can be restored using the reflog.

concepts.name: The Three Trees: Working Directory, Index, and HEAD
concepts.description: The Working Directory contains actual files on disk. The Index (Staging Area) holds the proposed next commit snapshot. HEAD points to the currently checked-out commit or branch tip.
concepts.production_usage: Knowing which tree is affected by commands (`git reset --soft`, `--mixed`, `--hard`) is critical to avoiding accidental data loss in production repositories.

concepts.name: Trunk-Based Development vs GitFlow
concepts.description: GitFlow utilizes long-lived feature, develop, release, and hotfix branches. Trunk-Based Development relies on short-lived feature branches merged frequently into main with feature flags.

concepts.name: Linux Kernel Isolation Primitives (Namespaces & cgroups)
concepts.description: Containers are simply standard Linux processes isolated via namespaces (PID, NET, MNT, IPC, UTS, USER) and resource-metered via cgroups (CPU bandwidth, memory limits, blkio).
concepts.production_usage: Demystifies container troubleshooting: a container process can be inspected directly on the host using standard host tools (`ps`, `top`, `nsenter`, `/proc/<PID>/`).

concepts.name: Multi-Stage Docker Builds & Image Layer Optimization
concepts.description: Separating compilation environments (compilers, SDKs, build tools) from the final minimal runtime image containing only the compiled artifact and runtime dependencies.
concepts.production_usage: Reduces image size by up to 90% (e.g. from 1.2GB down to 35MB for Go/Node.js apps), slashing deployment pull times and minimizing attack surface.

concepts.name: Overlay2 Union Filesystem & Copy-on-Write (CoW)
concepts.description: Layering immutable image layers (`lowerdir`) with an ephemeral container read-write layer (`upperdir`) merged through a virtual mount (`merged`).
concepts.production_usage: Heavy disk writes inside a container without volumes degrade performance due to CoW overhead and can exhaust host root partition storage.

concepts.name: Container Lifecycle & Signal Handling (PID 1 Problem)
concepts.description: The root process inside a container runs as PID 1. If not properly configured (e.g. using `tini` or direct `exec`), PID 1 will not forward SIGTERM to child processes, causing slow 10-second timeouts on shutdown.
concepts.production_usage: Ensuring zero-downtime rolling updates by allowing container processes to gracefully finish active requests upon receiving SIGTERM.

commands.troubleshooting: If logs are empty, the application may be writing directly to a file inside the container rather than to stdout/stderr.
commands.safe_practice: Configure Docker logging driver options (`max-size=50m`, `max-file=3`) in `/etc/docker/daemon.json` to prevent disk filling.

commands.company_usage: Live debugging of network connectivity, environment variables, or local configuration files inside a failing container.
commands.production_usage: Use sparingly in staging/dev environments to test network reachability to database backends.
commands.common_mistakes: Modifying application code or configuration permanently inside the container; all changes are lost when container restarts.
commands.troubleshooting: If `/bin/sh` or `/bin/bash` is not found, the container is distroless/scratch; use ephemeral debug containers or `nsenter` on the host.
commands.safe_practice: Do not install debugging tools or compile packages inside live production containers.
commands.challenge: Execute a diagnostic command inside a running container without opening an interactive shell.

options.description: Remove all unreferenced images, not just dangling ones.

commands.company_usage: Automated weekly maintenance on CI build runners to reclaim hundreds of gigabytes of disk space.
commands.production_usage: Run on CI worker nodes where hundreds of ephemeral test containers and images accumulate daily.
commands.common_mistakes: Running with `--volumes` in production environments where stateful database volumes are not actively mounted, permanently deleting data.
commands.troubleshooting: If prune hangs, the Docker daemon may be blocked on unmounting hung overlay2 mounts.

best_practices: Use minimal, secure base images (e.g. Distroless or Alpine Linux) to minimize vulnerability exposure.
Always enforce multi-stage Docker builds to separate compilation dependencies from runtime binaries.
Execute container processes as unprivileged non-root users (`USER 10001:10001`).
Set strict memory and CPU limits (`--memory`, `--cpus`) on all production containers.
Implement robust `HEALTHCHECK` directives to allow container orchestrators to detect deadlocked processes.

anti_patterns.name: Running as Root Inside Containers
anti_patterns.description: Defaulting to root user inside container images, increasing container breakout severity.
anti_patterns.remedy: Create an unprivileged user and group in the Dockerfile and declare `USER <non-root-uid>`.

anti_patterns.name: Storing Secrets in Docker Images
anti_patterns.description: Using `ENV API_KEY=secret` in a Dockerfile, baking secrets into immutable image layers.
anti_patterns.remedy: Pass secrets at runtime via environment variables or secret managers, or use Docker BuildKit `--mount=type=secret`.

anti_patterns.name: Using the 'latest' Image Tag in Production
anti_patterns.description: Deploying `app:latest`, making it impossible to know which version is running or rollback deterministically.
anti_patterns.remedy: Tag all images with immutable identifiers such as semantic versioning (`app:1.4.2`) or Git commit SHA (`app:sha-a1b2c3d`).

security_considerations: Scan all container images in CI/CD using automated scanners (Trivy, Grype) and block critical CVEs.
Drop all unnecessary Linux kernel capabilities (`--cap-drop=ALL --cap-add=NET_BIND_SERVICE`).
Run production containers with a read-only root filesystem (`--read-only`).
Sign container images cryptographically using Cosign and verify signatures before cluster deployment.

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: Container Exits Immediately with Code 137
troubleshooting_guide.root_cause: The container exceeded its configured memory limit and was terminated by the Linux Out-Of-Memory (OOM) Killer.
troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Run `docker inspect <container> --format '{{ .State.OOMKilled }}'`, check `dmesg -T | grep -i oom`.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Increase container memory limit or profile application heap memory consumption to fix memory leaks.

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: Docker Daemon Disk Full (Storage Driver Overlay2 Exhaustion)
troubleshooting_guide.root_cause: Accumulation of unused images, stopped containers, build caches, or unrotated container logs in `/var/lib/docker`.
troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Execute `docker system df` to inspect space breakdown between images, containers, and build cache.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Run `docker system prune -af` and configure max log size limits in `/etc/docker/daemon.json`.

concepts.name: Control Plane Architecture & etcd State Consistency
concepts.description: The control plane consists of kube-apiserver (REST API gateway), etcd (distributed consensus key-value store using Raft), kube-scheduler (assigns pods to nodes based on constraints), and kube-controller-manager (reconciliation loops).
concepts.production_usage: etcd latency directly dictates cluster performance. SREs must monitor fsync disk latency and maintain automated etcd snapshots before performing cluster upgrades.

concepts.name: Pod Lifecycle & Probe Mechanics (Startup, Liveness, Readiness)
concepts.description: Startup probes protect slow-starting legacy apps; Liveness probes kill and restart unresponsive containers; Readiness probes remove unhealthy pods from Service endpoints so they do not receive user traffic.
concepts.production_usage: Miscalibrated Liveness probes that point to heavy database queries cause cascading outages: under high load, queries slow down, probes fail, and Kubernetes restarts pods simultaneously.

concepts.name: Resource Quality of Service (QoS) Classes: Guaranteed, Burstable, BestEffort
concepts.description: Guaranteed pods have equal CPU/memory requests and limits. Burstable pods have requests lower than limits. BestEffort pods have no requests or limits specified.
concepts.production_usage: When a node encounters memory pressure, the kubelet evicts BestEffort pods first, then Burstable pods exceeding requests, protecting Guaranteed mission-critical workloads.

concepts.name: Helm 3 Architecture & Release Lifecycle
concepts.description: Package manager for Kubernetes using client-side templating (Go templates) and storing release state directly as Kubernetes Secrets within the target namespace, eliminating Tiller security vulnerabilities.
concepts.production_usage: Enterprise teams manage environment configurations (dev, staging, prod) via separate `values.yaml` files, enabling automated atomic rollouts with rollback capabilities.

commands.troubleshooting: If logs fail with 'container not found', wait for pod initialization or verify container name with `describe pod`.
commands.safe_practice: Ship logs to centralized logging (Loki, Elasticsearch) so historical crash logs persist after pod eviction.
commands.challenge: Write a command to stream logs concurrently from all pods matching the label `app=orders` across a cluster.

commands.common_mistakes: Rolling back a deployment without checking whether database schema migrations are backwards-compatible.
commands.troubleshooting: Use `kubectl rollout history` to inspect previous revisions before rolling back to verify the target revision contents.
commands.safe_practice: Always include the `--record` flag or maintain clean GitOps commit histories to keep track of revision changes.

commands.production_usage: Cordon the node first, then drain, allowing PodDisruptionBudgets to maintain minimum available application replicas.
commands.common_mistakes: Draining a node when workloads lack PodDisruptionBudgets (PDBs), leading to simultaneous termination of all service replicas.
commands.troubleshooting: If drain blocks indefinitely, a PodDisruptionBudget is preventing eviction; inspect with `kubectl get pdb -A`.
commands.safe_practice: Always verify application capacity and cluster spare resources before draining large worker nodes.
commands.challenge: Cordon a worker node, safely drain its workloads, verify pods reschedule to remaining nodes, and uncordon it.

commands.company_usage: Production continuous deployment stage in automated GitHub Actions and Jenkins pipelines.
commands.production_usage: Run in CI/CD deployment jobs with `--atomic` to ensure clusters never remain in a half-broken or inconsistent deployment state.
commands.common_mistakes: Omitting `--atomic` and `--timeout`, allowing broken releases to remain partially applied with pods failing silently.
commands.troubleshooting: If upgrade fails due to resource conflict, run `helm diff` or inspect existing resources for conflicting annotations.

best_practices: Always define CPU and memory requests and limits for every container to ensure predictable QoS classes.
Implement Startup, Liveness, and Readiness probes on all production workloads with conservative timeout settings.
Enforce PodDisruptionBudgets (PDBs) to maintain high availability during cluster maintenance and node draining.
Utilize NetworkPolicies to restrict traffic between namespaces and enforce microservice least-privilege networking.
Manage all manifests via Helm or Kustomize through GitOps workflows (ArgoCD or Flux) rather than direct manual kubectl apply.

anti_patterns.name: Omitting Resource Requests and Limits
anti_patterns.description: Deploying pods without CPU/memory specifications, resulting in BestEffort QoS and cluster instability.
anti_patterns.remedy: Enforce admission controllers (LimitRange or Kyverno) to mandate requests and limits on all pods.

anti_patterns.name: Heavy Database Queries in Liveness Probes
anti_patterns.description: Configuring liveness probes to execute full database SELECT queries, triggering cascading pod restart loops under load.
anti_patterns.remedy: Keep liveness probes shallow (simple HTTP 200 ping on /livez), and use readiness probes for dependency health.

anti_patterns.name: Storing Sensitive Data in Plaintext ConfigMaps
anti_patterns.description: Placing database passwords or API keys in standard ConfigMaps instead of external secrets managers.
anti_patterns.remedy: Use External Secrets Operator integrated with AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, or Google Secret Manager.

security_considerations: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted profile) to prohibit privileged containers and root users.
Implement strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) following least-privilege access principles.
Encrypt all Secrets at rest in etcd using KMS envelope encryption.
Restrict access to the Kubernetes API server using private VPC endpoints and authorized IP ranges.

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: Pod Stuck in CrashLoopBackOff
troubleshooting_guide.root_cause: Application process exits immediately after startup due to missing environment variables, DB connection error, or failed startup probe.
troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Execute `kubectl describe pod <name>` to view termination exit code, and `kubectl logs <name> --previous` to view crash logs.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Fix the missing ConfigMap/Secret key, correct startup probe timing, or resolve database network reachability.

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: Pod Stuck in Pending State (FailedScheduling)
troubleshooting_guide.root_cause: No node in the cluster has sufficient unallocated CPU/memory requests, or node affinity/taint constraints cannot be satisfied.
troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Run `kubectl describe pod <name>` and inspect the Events section for `0/N nodes are available: Insufficient cpu`.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Scale up cluster worker nodes (via Cluster Autoscaler / Karpenter) or right-size pod resource requests.

concepts.name: Declarative Graph Resolution & Dependency Engine
concepts.description: Terraform constructs a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of all resources, determines implicit and explicit dependencies (`depends_on`), and provisions non-dependent resources in parallel.
concepts.production_usage: Enables rapid provisioning of complex environments while guaranteeing proper sequencing (e.g. creating VPC before subnets, subnets before instances).

concepts.name: State Management & Distributed Locking
concepts.description: Terraform maps declarative code to real-world cloud resources via `terraform.tfstate`. Remote backends (S3 + DynamoDB) prevent concurrent writes via distributed locks.
concepts.production_usage: Prevents catastrophic state corruption when multiple engineers or automated CI runners execute plans simultaneously.

concepts.name: Infrastructure Drift & Refresh Mechanics

concepts.name: Immutable Infrastructure & Replacement Lifecycles
concepts.description: Replacing cloud instances or resources entirely rather than modifying them in-place, governed by lifecycle blocks (`create_before_destroy`, `prevent_destroy`).

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: Error Acquiring State Lock (ConditionalCheckFailedException)

troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Review the lock info (Lock ID, Owner, Path) printed in the error message and check running CI jobs.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: If the holding process has definitely terminated, release the lock using `terraform force-unlock <lock-id>`.

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: Resource Already Exists When Running Apply
troubleshooting_guide.root_cause: The resource was created out-of-band manually in the cloud console, but is absent from the Terraform state.
troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Identify the existing cloud identifier from the error message.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Import the existing resource using `terraform import <resource.address> <cloud-id>` or delete the manual resource.

concepts.name: Agentless Architecture & SSH Multiplexing

concepts.description: Tasks are designed such that applying them repeatedly ensures the target host matches the declared desired state without making redundant modifications or triggering unintended side effects.

concepts.name: Playbook Handlers & Change Notification
concepts.description: Handlers are specialized tasks that execute only once at the end of a play, and only if another task explicitly reported a `changed` state and notified the handler.
concepts.production_usage: Prevents redundant service restarts when updating configuration files (e.g. Nginx or PostgreSQL is restarted only when configuration content actually changed).

concepts.name: PromQL Vector Types & Rate Mechanics
concepts.description: Instant Vectors (single sample per series at a point in time), Range Vectors (range of samples over time, e.g. `[5m]`), and Scalar values. `rate()` calculates per-second average rate of increase for monotonically increasing counters, handling counter resets automatically.
concepts.production_usage: Never use `rate()` on Gauges (like memory or queue length); use `rate()` exclusively on Counters (like `http_requests_total`).

concepts.name: High Cardinality Pitfalls & Metric Relabeling
concepts.description: Cardinality is the total number of unique time series generated by the Cartesian product of label keys and values. Adding dynamic labels (e.g. user IDs, email addresses, order IDs) creates millions of series, crashing Prometheus with out-of-memory errors.
concepts.production_usage: Use `metric_relabel_configs` to drop or sanitize high-cardinality labels before ingestion, protecting Prometheus TSDB storage.

Implement multi-window multi-burn-rate alerting policies to prevent alert fatigue.
Correlate the Three Pillars of Observability (Metrics, Logs, and Traces) using unified trace and span IDs.

anti_patterns.name: High Cardinality Label Explosion
anti_patterns.description: Adding `user_id` or `order_id` as Prometheus metric labels, generating millions of series and crashing the TSDB.
anti_patterns.remedy: Store high-cardinality metadata in distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry) or structured logs (Loki), never in Prometheus labels.

anti_patterns.name: Alerting on Raw Spikes
anti_patterns.description: Configuring alerts that fire on a single 10-second spike, resulting in continuous false-alarm pages.
anti_patterns.remedy: Use rolling evaluation windows (`[5m]`) and require alerts to stay in breach state for a duration (`for: 5m`).

anti_patterns.name: Using rate() on Gauges
anti_patterns.description: Applying `rate()` to metrics that fluctuate up and down (like memory usage or thread count).
anti_patterns.remedy: Only use `rate()` on monotonically increasing Counters; use `avg_over_time()` or raw thresholds for Gauges.

security_considerations: Protect Prometheus and Alertmanager web endpoints with TLS and reverse proxy authentication.
Sanitize application metrics to guarantee no Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or secrets appear in label values.
Restrict access to Grafana dashboards using Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and enterprise SSO (SAML/OAuth).
Ensure distributed trace spans redact sensitive payload fields (passwords, credit card numbers).

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: Prometheus CrashLoopBackOff Due to OOM (Out Of Memory)
troubleshooting_guide.root_cause: A newly deployed service introduced high-cardinality metric labels, generating millions of active time series.
troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Inspect Prometheus startup logs, query `/api/v1/status/tsdb` for top cardinality labels.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Add `metric_relabel_configs` to drop the offending labels before ingestion and restart Prometheus with increased memory.

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: PromQL Query Timeouts in Grafana Dashboards
troubleshooting_guide.root_cause: Dashboard panels execute unaggregated queries across wide time ranges (`[30d]`) without recording rules.
troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Inspect Prometheus query log to identify long-running PromQL expressions exceeding 30 seconds.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Create Prometheus Recording Rules to precompute the metrics hourly and update dashboard panels to query the recorded series.

concepts.name: SLI, SLO, SLA & Error Budget Mechanics
concepts.description: Service Level Indicators (SLIs) measure real performance. Service Level Objectives (SLOs) set reliability targets agreed upon by engineering. Service Level Agreements (SLAs) are business contracts with financial penalties. Error Budget = 100% - SLO.
concepts.production_usage: When an error budget is exhausted, product feature deployments are frozen and all engineering capacity shifts to reliability and technical debt remediation.

concepts.name: Production Readiness Review (PRR) Framework
concepts.description: A formal audit conducted before onboarding or launching any new service into production, covering architecture, observability, scalability, failure modes, security, and operational runbooks.
concepts.production_usage: Guarantees that no service goes live without health checks, automated alerts, resource limits, on-call runbooks, and graceful degradation paths.

concepts.name: Blameless Postmortems & 5 Whys Root Cause Analysis
concepts.description: A culture and structured post-incident process assuming human operators do their best with the tools available. Focuses on systemic flaws, tooling gaps, and process deficiencies rather than individual blame.
concepts.production_usage: Drives continuous systemic improvement: turns every major production failure into high-priority engineering action items (P0/P1 fixes).

concepts.name: GitOps Architecture & Continuous Reconciliation
concepts.description: Operating model where Git is the single source of truth for desired infrastructure and application state. An automated agent (ArgoCD/Flux) continuously compares live state to Git state and automatically remediates drift.
concepts.production_usage: Eliminates configuration drift and prevents manual cluster tampering; all production changes are auditable Git pull requests.

anti_patterns.name: Punitive Postmortems & Finger Pointing
anti_patterns.description: Blaming individual engineers for human error during incidents, leading to culture of fear and hidden mistakes.
anti_patterns.remedy: Conduct blameless postmortems focusing on tooling, automated guardrails, system design, and organizational processes.

anti_patterns.name: Manual Production SSH Fixes
anti_patterns.description: SSHing into production servers to tweak configuration files manually without updating Git.
anti_patterns.remedy: Enforce GitOps: all changes must be committed to Git and deployed via automated pipelines.

anti_patterns.name: Ignoring Error Budget Depletion
anti_patterns.description: Continuing to ship risky feature releases even when the monthly error budget is completely exhausted.
anti_patterns.remedy: Enforce automated deployment freezes when error budget reaches zero until reliability fixes are deployed.

security_considerations: Enforce strict Separation of Duties: developers cannot deploy code to production without peer code review.
Require multi-factor authentication (MFA) and hardware security keys for all production infrastructure access.
Maintain immutable audit logs of all privileged access, deployment actions, and administrative commands.
Regularly test Disaster Recovery (DR) plans and offsite encrypted backup restoration procedures.

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: Cascading Microservice Outage Under Traffic Surge
troubleshooting_guide.root_cause: Downstream dependency failure caused request queues to back up, exhausting thread pools across all calling services.
troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Inspect distributed traces to identify the slowest bottleneck service and check connection pool exhaustion metrics.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Engage circuit breakers, enable aggressive timeouts, and return graceful cached fallback responses.

troubleshooting_guide.failure_mode: GitOps Drift Storm (Continuous Out-Of-Sync State)
troubleshooting_guide.root_cause: An external mutating admission controller or human operator is modifying live resources in conflict with Git.
troubleshooting_guide.diagnostic_workflow: Run `argocd app diff <app>` to identify which fields are continuously oscillating.
troubleshooting_guide.remediation_procedure: Align the Git repository manifest with the mutated fields or configure `ignoreDifferences` in ArgoCD application spec.
